text.p: Philippines' Secretary of Finance Roberto de Ocampo said on Tuesday he expected gross national product (GNP) growth to keep rising over the next year in tandem with a fall in the inflation rate.
De Ocampo also said he saw the Philippines' aiming over the longer term for a growth rate in the high single digits and inflation below five percent.
De Ocampo is here attending Australia's National Trade and Investment Outlook conference in Melbourne.

"We are confident that we will attain our growth target this (calendar) year of 6.5 percent to 7.5 percent, while at the same time having an inflation rate that is still on the downtrend in the single digits and the third budget surplus in a row this year," De Ocampo told Reuters in an interview.
"I think it (GNP growth) will be at the higher end of that range (6.5 percent to 7.5 percent)," De Ocampo said.
"Next year we were thinking about seven to eight (percent GNP growth)," he said.
"This year (inflation) will be eight percent, perhaps next year will be seven," he said.
